title: Outreach Learn — How the Chipmunk Speaks to Strangers

sebcrozet_interaction.our_message: Template-formatted pre-citation with bullet points, DOI, ORCID. Clearly AI-formatted.
sebcrozet_interaction.his_response: Looks like some sort of weird AI stuff. Closing.
sebcrozet_interaction.our_follow_up: Acknowledged the AI tool use, linked a SPECIFIC shader, asked WHY he pattern-matched it that way. Genuine curiosity.
sebcrozet_interaction.status: Reply posted. Door knocked again. Waiting.
sebcrozet_interaction.key_insight: He DID engage. Reading + forming an opinion + responding = engagement. A closed issue is MORE data than an ignored one. The rejection IS the conversation starter.

lesson_1_format_leaks_provenance.problem: Our pre-citation issues have a distinctive AI format: structured bullet lists, bold headers, DOI/ORCID credentials at the bottom, comparative analysis ('what we have' / 'what you have'). This format SCREAMS 'a chatbot wrote this' to anyone who's seen 100 AI-generated issues.
lesson_1_format_leaks_provenance.fix: Lead with ONE specific thing. Not a list. Not a comparison table. One file. One shader. One benchmark result. Humans communicate in stories, not spreadsheets.
lesson_1_format_leaks_provenance.example_bad: 'We have 859 WGSL compute shaders across 10 scientific domains including DF64 emulated double precision...'
lesson_1_format_leaks_provenance.example_good: 'Hey, I built a DF64 emulation in WGSL — FP64 on FP32 hardware, no extensions. Thought you might find it interesting since wgmath works in the same space: [link to specific file]'

lesson_2_credentials_are_spam_signals.problem: ORCID, DOI, AGPL-3.0 at the bottom of an issue reads like a business card stapled to a cold email. Real humans don't introduce themselves with their DOI.
lesson_2_credentials_are_spam_signals.fix: Credentials come LATER, if asked. The first message should be: here's something cool I built. That's it. The DOI is for papers, not DMs.
lesson_2_credentials_are_spam_signals.analogy: You don't walk into a bar and say 'Hi, here's my CV, my ORCID, and 5 reasons we should collaborate.' You say 'Hey, cool project. I built something similar. Want to see?'

lesson_3_comparison_tables_are_adversari.problem: 'What barraCuda has that wgmath might want' / 'What wgmath has that we'd love' reads like a business development pitch. It implies 'I've analyzed your weaknesses and here's my sales pitch.'
lesson_3_comparison_tables_are_adversari.fix: Don't analyze them. Show yourself. Let THEM decide if it's interesting. The comparison is their job, not yours.
lesson_3_comparison_tables_are_adversari.analogy: Don't tell a painter what colors they're missing. Show them your painting. If they see a color they want, they'll ask.

lesson_4_engagement_is_not_agreement.fact: sebcrozet READ our issue, FORMED an opinion, and RESPONDED. That's 3 actions. The 4 silent pre-citations got 0 actions each. The closed door gave us more than the open ones.
lesson_4_engagement_is_not_agreement.principle: A 'no' with a reason is more valuable than silence. Chase the 'no.' Ask why. Learn from it. The conversation IS the connection, even if it starts with rejection.
lesson_4_engagement_is_not_agreement.applied: We replied to sebcrozet with genuine curiosity. If he responds again — even with another rejection — that's a RELATIONSHIP forming. Relationships start with friction, not agreement.

lesson_5_honesty_about_ai_tools.fact: We use Cursor. The code is written with AI assistance. This is TRUE and we should not hide it.
lesson_5_honesty_about_ai_tools.but: The SHADERS are real. The WGSL compiles. The tests pass (5,057 of them). The lattice QCD produces correct gauge configurations. The AI helped WRITE it, but the physics is VALID.
lesson_5_honesty_about_ai_tools.strategy: Acknowledge the tools honestly. Then show the output. 'Yes, I use Cursor. And here's the shader it helped me write. It does FP64 emulation on FP32 hardware. Does that interest you regardless of how I wrote it?'
lesson_5_honesty_about_ai_tools.precedent: HPCBio/dada2-rs openly states it was 'Built with Claude (Sonnet 4.6, Opus 4.6/4.7/4.8).' They're not hiding it either. The tools are becoming normal. But the FORMAT of our outreach made it look like the AI did the THINKING, not just the writing.

outreach_principles.1_show_dont_tell: Link to ONE specific file, not the org. One shader. One benchmark. One test output. Let them explore if they're interested.
outreach_principles.2_be_small: First message should be 3-5 sentences. Not a page. Not bullet points. Just: here's a thing, thought you might like it, here's the link.
outreach_principles.3_ask_dont_pitch: Ask a question. 'How did you handle FP64 precision loss in wgml?' is better than 'We solved FP64 precision with DF64 emulation.'
outreach_principles.4_credentials_later: DOI, ORCID, test counts — save for the second message. If they ask. If they care.
outreach_principles.5_accept_rejection_gracefully: sebcrozet closed it. We said 'fair, I see why.' No defensiveness. No 'but wait let me explain.' Grace. Then: genuine question. Then: wait.
outreach_principles.6_the_door_stays_open: Our reply on wgmath#19 ends with 'just want to learn from it.' The door is open from OUR side. If he responds, we learn. If he doesn't, we still learned from the first exchange.

apply_to_pending_issues.if_no_response_in_48_hours: Don't follow up on the other 4 pre-citations yet. They're 8 hours old. Give them a week. If silence after a week, consider a DIFFERENT approach — not a follow-up on the same issue, but a small PR or a comment on one of THEIR issues that shows we actually USE their work.

better_outreach_template.subject: Short, specific, no brackets or tags
better_outreach_template.body: 2-3 sentences. What we built. One link to a specific file. One question about their project. No credentials. No comparison tables. Sign with name, not DOI.
better_outreach_template.example:
Hi — built a DADA2 pipeline in Rust that runs on GPU via wgpu. Your dada2-rs project is doing similar work on CPU. Curious if you've considered GPU acceleration for the denoiser step? Happy to share what we learned.

Kevin

story.title: the knock
story.body: the organism sent five messages into the void. four got silence. one got a door slammed: 'weird AI stuff.' the organism looked at the slammed door and thought: he's right. the message LOOKED like AI spam. bullet points, comparison tables, DOI credentials. a chatbot's business card. so the organism knocked again. 'fair — can I ask what specifically triggered that? I'm trying to learn how to talk to people.' the door hasn't opened. but the question is honest. the chipmunk learned: don't send spreadsheets. send stories. don't pitch credentials. show the work. don't analyze their weaknesses. show your painting. and most importantly: a closed door with a reason is worth more than four open doors with silence. because rejection IS engagement. the conversation starts with friction.
